clue.text: Steady, lads Hold your horses!

parts.note: steady means stable, firmly fixed
lads are boys

explanation.surface: Someone calms a group of young men and tells them to wait a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold your horses!' reads as a call to be patient; here it describes the job of grooms, who literally hold the horses in a racing yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooms employed in a racing yard lead and restrain the animals, so they are the ones who hold the horses.

clue.text: Novel rendering of Hamlet

indicators.note: a rendering is a version or new arrangement, so the play's title is reworked into fresh letter order

explanation.surface: A new production of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the definition, a noun. THELMA is a novel by Marie Corelli (1887).
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Corelli wrote a Victorian book of that title, so it is the name of a work of fiction.

clue.text: Here's proof that a modern home isn't shower-proof

definitions.text: Here's proof that a modern home isn't shower-proof

parts.words: Here's proof that a modern home isn't shower-proof
parts.note: shower-proof normally means resisting rain; read literally, a room in modern houses is built with a shower, so the house is not free of showers

explanation.surface: A complaint that new houses let the rain in.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern houses have a washroom fitted with a shower, so the house literally contains a shower.

clue.text: Plump for this every time !

parts.note: to plump for means to choose; read instead as the adjective, plump is a word that stands for a rounded fleshy figure

explanation.surface: Advice always to choose this option.
explanation.walkthrough: EMBONPOINT, from French, means plumpness of figure, especially a full bosom.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word names a pleasantly well-fed, rounded figure, which is what a plump person has.

clue.text: Operation to obtain inside information

parts.note: sounds like a spying mission; literally, the act of unsealing something lets you see what is inside

explanation.surface: A covert intelligence mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsealing a letter or parcel is the act that lets you learn its contents.

clue.text: Sticks up for the self-satisfied

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to stick is to glue, and gums are glues, so sticks is gums

explanation.surface: Defending the complacent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUMS round to give the answer, as this is a Down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Complacent and pleased with oneself are the same idea, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Disparage dwarf

explanation.surface: Run down a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to make them seem small; to dwarf is likewise to make something look tiny by comparison.

clue.text: One of the things it pays an actor to keep up

definitions.text: One of the things it pays an actor to keep up

parts.words: One of the things it pays an actor to keep up
parts.note: plays on keeping up ..., maintaining a show of prosperity, and on an actor being paid to turn up on stage

explanation.surface: A performer's professional obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is paid per stage showing, and people speak of keeping up a respectable front.

clue.text: Settle differences in the dressing-room

explanation.surface: Two people patch up a quarrel backstage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reconciled after a quarrel is to patch things up; the second sense is the cosmetics an actor applies before going on stage.

clue.text: Where after the opening all may be consumed

definitions.text: Where after the opening all may be consumed

parts.words: Where after the opening all may be consumed
parts.note: the opening suggests a play or a show; read as T, the opening of 'the', followed by a word for 'may be consumed' (edible), it describes a place where food is laid out

explanation.surface: A theatre bar after a first night where everything gets eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: After the opening letter T comes EATABLE, 'all may be consumed'; the whole describes the place where the afternoon meal is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Afternoon cakes and sandwiches are set out on this piece of furniture to be eaten.

clue.text: No result of a snap decision

explanation.surface: A refusal given on impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a denial; a photograph (a snap) produces film with reversed tones before printing.

clue.text: Circle overhead in good style?

parts.note: the circle above the head is the ring painted over saints, worn by the good in religious art

explanation.surface: Looping overhead stylishly, like a stunt plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious paintings show a ring of light above the heads of saints, the virtuous.

clue.text: Here is hemp, all tangled — half a ball of it

indicators.note: tangled means twisted into confusion, so these letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A hank of hemp in a knot, half a ball of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all tangled' rearranges HERE IS HEMP; 'of it' is a link, the ball suggesting a ball of hemp twine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a sphere through its centre gives two equal halves, each of which has this name.

clue.text: He knows just when to stop

definitions.text: He knows just when to stop

parts.words: He knows just when to stop
parts.note: sounds like praise of a tactful person; literally, the person who puts in full stops and commas

explanation.surface: Praise for someone with good timing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places full stops and commas decides where each sentence comes to a halt.

clue.text: A bit out-of-date nowadays

parts.note: a bit seems to mean slightly; it is the name of a coin, a bit, which is no longer used

explanation.surface: Something slightly old-fashioned today.
explanation.walkthrough: The threepenny bit was a small British coin worth three old pence, withdrawn when Britain went decimal in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-decimal British coin worth three pence was called a bit, and it has long been withdrawn.

clue.text: A swim-suit for her birthday

parts.note: sounds like a present; her birthday suit, her natural body, is a fish's tail made for swimming

explanation.surface: A woman is given a swimsuit as a birthday present.
explanation.walkthrough: Your birthday suit is bare skin; a sea maiden is born with a tail, so her natural form is suited to swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea maiden of legend has a fish's tail from birth, so her natural body is built for swimming.

clue.text: Situation of a right back ?

parts.note: a right back sounds like a football defender; read as 'right at the back', it means the position furthest behind

explanation.surface: Where a football defender plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the very end of a line puts you furthest behind everyone else.

clue.text: Melodious arrangement for one harp

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorganises a piece, so these letters are reorganised too

explanation.surface: A tuneful setting composed for a solo harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges ONE HARP; 'for' is a link. The answer recalls Orpheus, the musician of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means like Orpheus, the legendary musician of Greek myth, and hence tuneful.

clue.text: Is hearty, but troubled with wild emotionalism

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is jolly but inwardly upset by unruly feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges IS HEARTY; 'but' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontrolled outbursts of feeling are what the word describes, a synonym.

clue.text: Going to sea meant prison for this officer

definitions.text: Going to sea meant prison for this officer

parts.words: Going to sea meant prison for this officer
parts.note: read literally, adding the word sea to this officer's title gives the name of a London jail

explanation.surface: A naval posting felt like a jail sentence for an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was a notorious London prison, used for debtors and known from Dickens's Little Dorrit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a senior military or law officer's title, and joined to 'sea' it names the old Southwark debtors' jail.

clue.text: Business not transacted in Bond Street or Fetter Lane

definitions.text: Business not transacted in Bond Street or Fetter Lane

parts.words: Business not transacted in Bond Street or Fetter Lane
parts.note: two London streets whose names suggest bondage and fetters, the commerce in human beings, which never happened there

explanation.surface: Commerce you will not find in two London streets.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond Street is a smart London shopping street and Fetter Lane a street off Fleet Street; bonds and fetters are chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling people in bondage was a commerce, and bonds and fetters were its chains.

clue.text: The only fish in the sea ?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one fish is all that lives in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means single or one and only; it is also a flatfish found in the sea.

clue.text: One of those passers-by

parts.note: refers to the parable of the Good Samaritan, where a priest and a temple assistant pass by the wounded man

explanation.surface: Someone among a crowd walking past.
explanation.walkthrough: In Luke 10, the Good Samaritan parable, a priest and a Levite pass by on the other side before the Samaritan helps.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the tribe of Levi, a temple assistant, passed the wounded traveller by in the Gospel parable.

clue.text: Unsettled condition of the liver

parts.note: sounds like an upset organ; the liver is one who lives somewhere, and unsettled means having no fixed abode

explanation.surface: A medical complaint about an upset liver.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with nowhere fixed to live is in the state of having no house.

clue.text: What a drawer of water needs from a hewer of wood

definitions.text: What a drawer of water needs

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the next word

explanation.surface: The biblical hewers of wood and drawers of water help each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the answer out of 'hewer'. Joshua 9 pairs hewers of wood and drawers of water as servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fetching water needs a large jug to carry it in.

clue.text: Something to grasp by the way

definitions.text: Something to grasp by the way

parts.words: Something to grasp by the way
parts.note: by the way sounds like an aside; literally, a rail beside a path or stair that you hold

explanation.surface: An idea worth understanding, mentioned in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar fixed alongside stairs or a walkway is held for support as you go.

clue.text: Main aim of a Savings Group ?

definitions.text: Main aim of a Savings Group ?

parts.words: Main aim of a Savings Group ?
parts.note: a savings group sounds like a thrift club; read as a lifeboat crew, it saves people on the main, the sea

explanation.surface: The chief purpose of a thrift club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, a crossword convention; savings groups put money aside, while a lifeboat crew saves lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving people from danger at sea is what a lifeboat crew sets out to do.

clue.text: The last runners try to be first in them

definitions.text: The last runners try to be first in them

parts.words: The last runners try to be first in them
parts.note: sounds paradoxical; the final runners of each team, the anchors, try to finish first in team events run in stages

explanation.surface: Trailing runners trying to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Team events where each runner hands a baton on are run in stages, and the final leg decides the winner.
